summary: Seven small skills: one session governs while background agents take each goal through a built-in idea, plan, review, test and ship routine, or your own skills, to a pull request, unattended, and keep a wiki, regression tests, releases and repo health in check. Runs on Claude Code and Codex.
use_cases: Take one sentence to a pull request through your own skills
Run several goals in parallel and see what waits on you
Cut a draft GitHub release with a changelog
Adopt a new or existing repo in one command, and update the skills later
Keep a GitHub wiki in the repo and find stale pages
Check a repo's health with fixed rules
Keep regression tests visible, with an issue per failure
writes: .loop/config.json, .loop/queue.md, .loop/findings.md, .loop/goals/<slug>.md in the repo
run state under the git common dir, in loop/ (never committed)
git worktrees under that loop/ folder
git branches loop/<slug> and workflow-setup, commits on them
.git/hooks/pre-commit, commit-msg and pre-push in a repo, only when setup.py --git-hooks or a default setup run installs the private-name scan (never overwriting a hook that is not ours)
VERSION and CHANGELOG.md on a goal's branch when you cut
.loop/docs.tsv and docs/wiki/*.md on a branch
pages it wrote, or that you name, in the repo's GitHub wiki, when you publish
.loop/regression.tsv, .loop/regression-known.tsv and .github/workflows/regression.yml
a version bump commit on a goal's branch, only with pr_bumps_version on

loop/board.json, cadence and handoff.md under the git common dir, and a run record's note, retired mark, report or met lines, and loop/checkin.json (the last check-in time), when you run board.py, worker.py or operate.py

loop/session-pool.json (the worker session pool), its lock file loop/session-pool.json.lock, and a run record's worker, session and reports, when you run sessions.py, watch.py or mend.py; and the session tool named in session_command, called as start, rename and send
loop/board.html, board-artifact.html and the finished sections of board.json, when you run board_page.py
loop/waits/<slug> under the git common dir, when a goal is held by another
~/.workflow-loop/repos in the home folder, when you run board.py repos add

~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.workflow-loop.schedule.plist and ~/.workflow-loop/schedule/ (registry, log, checkouts), when you run automation.py local install; nothing is loaded until you run the launchctl line it prints
docs/wiki/*.md and a commit of them, when you run criteria.py review, unreview or render
.loop/regression-runs.tsv, when you run regression.py run
issues labelled regression or health, and milestones on them, on GitHub, only with --live or a token
reads ~/.workflow-loop/flow.json, and runs its probe and its command for each flow step; record reads its full_markers, and each step's depth goes into the run record and the pull request body
a merge of a goal's pull request into the base branch, only with auto_merge on, when you run merge.py
a feature page for each top-level code folder and Home, .loop/docs.tsv and .loop/regression.tsv rows, on the workflow-setup branch
the installed skill files and workflow-package.json in the skills folder, only when you run update.py --apply
network: github.com (git push, wiki push, gh pull request, issue, milestone and draft release calls, only when you run them)
the model host your own claude or codex command already uses
api.cloudflare.com (Cloudflare Email Service send API, from the scheduled health run on your Mac only, with the CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL_TOKEN you put in the schedule's mail.env)
your smtp_host (default smtp.gmail.com), from the scheduled health run on your Mac only, when digest_mail is smtp
requires: a background agent command such as claude or codex, for go and watch
gh, signed in, for pull requests, issues and releases
optionally your own skill suite, named in ~/.workflow-loop/flow.json (setup fills it with the built-in flow)
limitations: Regression runs each row's command through a shell, so Agensi's scan flags shell=True in regression.py, actions.py and defect.py.
The regression workflow command writes a small runner into the repo, so the Actions run needs no skill files.
Each background agent needs its own access to these skills, and scripts that call a sibling script need them on disk: mending, and health's criteria and docs rules, say so and skip otherwise.
This repo itself runs with no gates: no check step, auto-approval and auto-merge. A new repo keeps auto-approval and auto-merge off until its owner turns them on.
